name: Small-data DuckDB stack
description: The anti-big-data stack: dlt pulls sources into Parquet files or MotherDuck, DuckDB provides a shockingly fast single-node SQL engine, dbt (via the duckdb adapter) gives the same modelling discipline as any warehouse stack, and Evidence renders BI as code. Total infrastructure: roughly none — pipelines run on a laptop, a cron box, or CI. The insight it operationalizes is that the overwhelming majority of analytical datasets are under a few hundred gigabytes, where a modern single node outperforms distributed systems while costing nothing and debugging trivially. Because the shape mirrors the modern data stack (EL, store, dbt, BI), graduating to blueprint 2 later is a migration, not a rewrite. Raw tables inside the single store act as the landing layer; a separate lake would be overkill at this scale.
when_to_use: Choose this when data fits comfortably on one machine (up to low-hundreds of GB), the team is small, and speed-to-answer beats platform-building — startups, internal analytics, departmental reporting, data products with bounded scope.
It is also the right sandbox for validating models before paying for a warehouse.
Your data fits on one machine and your team fits in one room.
when_not_to_use: Outgrow it when data or concurrency does: many simultaneous BI users, always-on query APIs, or TB-scale scans point at a warehouse or lakehouse.
Compliance regimes that demand centralized access control and audit trails fit a governed warehouse better than files.
And if five teams need to share and write concurrently, single-node DuckDB's write model becomes the constraint — MotherDuck softens this, but only so far.

hot_spots.title: Single-node limits
hot_spots.detail: One box means one failure domain and a hard ceiling you hit suddenly.

hot_spots.title: Write concurrency
hot_spots.detail: Embedded databases dislike many simultaneous writers.

hot_spots.title: Growing up
hot_spots.detail: Success outgrows the stack; plan the graduation path before you need it.

evolution.reason: You outgrew one machine — keep the SQL-first workflow, add managed scale.

stages.name: Ingest
stages.role: Pull APIs, databases, and files into local/cloud storage with schema handling
stages.rationale: dlt is pip-installable Python that runs wherever the rest of this stack does — no connector server, no containers — with declarative schema evolution and native DuckDB/Parquet/MotherDuck destinations. That zero-infrastructure fit is the whole game here. Airbyte or Meltano make sense only if you need a connector dlt lacks and would rather run their machinery than write one; Singer taps are the raw-materials fallback.

stages.name: Store
stages.role: Hold raw and modelled data: local Parquet/DuckDB files, or MotherDuck for a shared cloud endpoint
stages.rationale: MotherDuck is DuckDB-as-a-service — a shared, always-on endpoint that solves the two things files on a laptop cannot: team access and BI tools needing somewhere to connect, while keeping DuckDB's cost profile. Pure-local DuckDB over Parquet files (optionally synced to S3) is even simpler and perfectly right for a solo analyst or CI-driven builds; Parquet as the interchange format keeps everything readable by any future engine, which is your painless exit path either way.

stages.name: Transform
stages.role: dbt models executed by DuckDB via the dbt-duckdb adapter — 'dbt-duckdb' has no separate corpus slug, so dbt is the entry
stages.rationale: dbt with the dbt-duckdb adapter gives this tiny stack grown-up habits — tests, docs, lineage, environments — and a model layer that ports to Snowflake or BigQuery nearly unchanged when you graduate; the adapter's ability to read Parquet/S3 directly and write external files is a quiet superpower. SQLMesh also runs beautifully on DuckDB with stronger incremental semantics and is arguably the better greenfield choice for engineer-led teams. Polars covers the transformations that are more naturally dataframe code than SQL.

stages.name: BI
stages.role: Publish reports and dashboards from the modelled data as static, versioned pages
stages.rationale: Evidence renders markdown-plus-SQL into fast static sites — BI as code in the same repo as the dbt models, deployable anywhere, no server to run, which matches this stack's zero-infrastructure ethos exactly. Metabase is the pick when non-technical users need to self-serve and click around rather than read published pages (point it at MotherDuck). Streamlit when reports become interactive apps; Lightdash when you want dbt-metric-driven exploration.
